components-form-layout-editfooter.description: Render the action footer for an edit session.

dirty.description: Whether the form diverges from the entity the server last returned.

saving.description: A save is in flight — locks both actions.

disabled.description: Lock both actions regardless of `dirty` (e.g. the form is still loading).

canSubmit.description:
Extra Save gate, as `EditorActions.canSubmit`: false while a required field is
 missing. Save then says so instead of saving; Cancel can still discard. Default `true`.

saved.description:
The last save succeeded and nothing changed since — e.g. `useEntityEditor().saved`.
 Without it a clean form stays silent: no status on entering a form.

onSave.description: Fired only with something to save and nothing missing.

onCancel.description: Discard edits. Fired only when there is something to discard.

sx.description:
Applied after every default, so a host can restyle the band — including
 `backgroundImage: 'none'` to drop the dirty tint.

components-form-layout-formsections.name: Demo

param: {FormSectionsProps} props the sections, the field renderer, the column-3 aside, the TOC's label, the section labels and the footer
returns: {JSX.Element} the laid-out form body, with its TOC and aside when it has them

components-form-layout-formsections.description:
Stacked form sections on a 12-column grid, each field as wide as its resolved
`width` from `sm` up. One section renders flat, with no heading. With a table
of contents' worth of sections (`tocSections`) it also draws the `SectionToc`:
a sticky column on the right from `lg` up, a dropdown above the form below it,
linked to scrolling both ways through `useSectionSpy`. An `aside` stacks above
the TOC in that column. From `lg` up, in a host of fixed height (a form page), the
form column and column 3 each scroll on their own: picture and TOC stay put while the
form, its `footer` sticking to the bottom, scrolls (#293).

components-icons-transportmodeicon.description:
Render a NeTEx TransportMode glyph. Backed by the inline SVG sprite in
{@link TransportModeSprite}. Three rendering modes:

- `iconPosition` omitted → icon only with tooltip + `aria-label`
- `iconPosition === 'left'`  → `[icon] [label]`
- `iconPosition === 'right'` → `[label] [icon]`

The visible / tooltip label comes from the existing `transportMode.*`
i18n keys via {@link transportModeLabelKey}. No `label` prop override —
the locale bundle is the single source of truth.

data-deck-plans-deckrendering.name: DeckRendering
data-deck-plans-deckrendering.description:
Read-only SVG rendering of a single deck, backed by the editor package's
`<deck-rendering>` custom element.

The element is created and populated imperatively rather than written as
JSX. Vue renders custom elements in `connectedCallback`, and the component's
`stageSize` dereferences `deck.getBoundingBox()` on that first pass — so a
React-inserted element would throw before any effect could assign `deck`.
Creating it detached, assigning props, then inserting sidesteps that and
removes the need to augment `JSX.IntrinsicElements`.

Renders nothing until the bundle has loaded; callers own the loading UI.
A mount that throws reports itself in place rather than rendering nothing,
which would read as "this deck is empty" while the strip around it looks
healthy. In practice `DeckStrip` catches a failed bundle load first, so that
branch is a guard for standalone use (the stories mount this directly), not
a path the app reaches.

Styling is applied after insertion and cannot fail the rendering — see
`deckRenderingStyles`.

Stories for the Home dashboard. A MemoryRouter decorator supplies the routing
context the page's <Link>s need (`Complete` brings its own router); `withOrganisations` and `withAuth` stand in
for the real OrganisationsProvider and OIDC provider (config/fetch-driven, so

`fullscreen` layout lets the flat, full-width
dashboard breathe without Storybook's default padding. Domain glyphs come from
the nav-rail MenuIcon sprite, mounted globally in `.storybook/preview.tsx`.
